jobs.occupation: Global Head of Strategy & Real Estate (Fachwirt/in - Facility-Management)
jobs.description: Work Your Magic with us!Ready to explore, break barriers, and discover more? We know you’ve got big plans – so do we! Our colleagues across the globe love innovating with science and technology to enrich people’s lives with our solutions in Healthcare, Life Science, and Electronics. Together, we dream big and are passionate about caring for our rich mix of people, customers, patients, and planet. That's why we are always looking for curious minds that see themselves imagining the unimaginable with us.This is one of the most strategically significant roles in the new CREM structure — and in many respects the strategic right hand of the Head of CREM. Portfolio strategy, proactive planning and workplace strategy do not currently exist in a mature form within Merck's real estate organisation — you will establish them. Transactions capability exists and is largely retained; your mandate is to elevate it from reactive execution to strategically-led delivery.KEY RESPONSIBILITIES- Portfolio Strategy: Lead the development and annual refresh of CREM's Real Estate Plan of Record — translating business growth, consolidation and transformation requirements into a multi-year portfolio strategy with clear priorities, scenarios and business cases. Own portfolio optimisation as the function's primary strategic output.- Business Partnering: Serve as a senior strategic partner to business sector leads across Healthcare, Life Science and Electronics — embedding CRE into business planning cycles before decisions are made, not after. Maintain sufficient transaction expertise to provide cover and resource flexibility where needed.- Portfolio Management Oversight: Direct the regional Portfolio Managers in building and maintaining portfolio performance visibility, opportunity identification and Plan of Record delivery across all geographies.- Governance & Process: Champion the adoption of CREM's transaction and strategy governance frameworks — ensuring compliance with playbooks, approval processes and decision rights across the team. Responsible for approving all global real estate transactions above approved thresholds- Stakeholder Engagement: Represent CREM in cross-functional forums alongside the Head of CREM — including OLC engagement, sector strategy sessions and M&A workstreams where real estate input is required.QUALIFICATIONS- 12+ years in corporate real estate, with a strong track record in portfolio strategy, location strategy or strategic business partnering at a senior level within a large multinational- Demonstrated experience developing and owning portfolio strategy — scenario planning, multi-year planning, lease expiry management, location strategy- Strong commercial acumen with the ability to build and present compelling business cases to C-suite audiences- Deep understanding of transaction management across leasehold and freehold assets; sufficient execution expertise to provide leadership continuity across the regional transaction teams- Experience working in a matrixed, multi-sector corporate environment; comfortable navigating complex stakeholder landscapes- Exceptional relationship builder — able to operate credibly at senior business and executive level- Exposure to workplace strategy and occupancy planning advantageous- Master's degree in Real Estate, Business Administration, Finance or a related field- Fluency in English required; additional languages advantageous given global remitWhat we offer: We are curious minds that come from a broad range of backgrounds, perspectives, and life experiences. We are committed to creating access and opportunities for all to develop and grow at your own pace. Join us in building a culture of inclusion and belonging that impacts millions and empowers everyone to work their magic and champion human progress!Apply now and become a part of a team that is dedicated to Sparking Discovery and Elevating Humanity!

jobs.occupation: PhD Position on Femtosecond Spectroscopy of Chiral Molecular Ions (Wissenschaftliche/r Mitarbeiter/in)
jobs.description: Job available in 2 locations: Bremen, KasselWork ScheduleStandard (Mon-Fri)Environmental ConditionsOfficeJob DescriptionA PhD position is available in Germany within the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network TRILOGY, funded under Horizon Europe. The selected doctoral candidate will work on an interdisciplinary research project focused on ultrafast spectroscopy of chiral molecular ions, combining expertise in physics, chemistry, engineering, mass spectrometry, and ultrafast science.The position is offered through a collaboration between the University of Kassel and Thermo Fisher Scientific. The doctoral researcher will be employed by Thermo Fisher Scientific for the full three-year duration of the PhD project. The doctoral thesis will be supervised by Prof. Dr. Jochen Mikosch at the University of Kassel. During the first 24 months, the doctoral researcher will be based at Thermo Fisher Scientific in Bremen, Germany. This will be followed by an 12-month research period at the University of Kassel.About the TRILOGY Doctoral NetworkTRILOGY is a Horizon Europe MSCA Doctoral Network advancing research in the emerging field of ultrafast chirality. The network aims to exploit attosecond light-driven electron dynamics to overcome limitations associated with conventional chiroptical methods.The research targets potential applications in life sciences and advanced technologies, with the goal of developing next-generation, highly sensitive spectroscopic tools for studying chiral molecules.The network brings together institutions and partners from across Europe and will train 16 doctoral candidates at the intersection of experimental and theoretical ultrafast science. Researchers will work in an interdisciplinary environment spanning physics, chemistry, engineering, and related areas while gaining experience through collaboration between academia and industry.The PhD project in Germany contributes to the TRILOGY work package focused on the design, development, and testing of an instrument for chiral photoelectron spectroscopy of molecular ions.About the PhD ProjectThe selected candidate will conduct research on the ultrafast spectroscopy of chiral molecular ions.The project will involve close collaboration between the University of Kassel and Thermo Fisher Scientific, a company active in the field of mass spectrometry.During the first approximately 24 months, the main workplace will be at Thermo Fisher Scientific in Bremen. The researcher will work on adapting an electrospray ion source and related instrumentation.The researcher will subsequently relocate to the University of Kassel to perform experiments involving chiral molecular ions and femtosecond laser pulses. The experiments will use a novel momentum spectrometer ion target developed at the University of Kassel together with the ion source developed in collaboration with Thermo Fisher Scientific.Key Research Activities- The doctoral candidate will take a leading role in several research and technical activities, including:- Adapting the hardware and software of a high-resolution Orbitrap Mass Spectrometer equipped with an electrospray ion source and radiofrequency-based ion trap or ion accumulation system.- Developing an ion guide transfer system for extracting molecular ions to an external spectrometer.- Establishing protocols for producing and accumulating negatively charged chiral molecular ions of pharmaceutical relevance.- Conducting ion-optical simulations to optimize ion trap performance and improve ion accumulation efficiency.- Integrating the experimental control systems of the adapted Orbitrap Mass Spectrometer and the home-built momentum spectrometer at the University of Kassel.- Performing, analyzing, interpreting, and publishing Photoelectron Circular Dichroism (PECD) photo-detachment experiments involving negatively charged chiral molecular ions and femtosecond laser pulses.- Exploring opportunities to translate fundamental research in atomic, molecular, and optical physics into real-world applications.- The selected researcher will also collaborate closely with international partners across the TRILOGY consortium and undertake two funded research stays with partner organizations within the network.- Through the program, the doctoral candidate will have opportunities to strengthen their research profile through scientific publications, conference presentations, collaborative project activities, and interaction with academic and industrial researchers across Europe.Candidate ProfileApplicants should have:- A Master's degree or equivalent in physics, engineering, chemistry, or a related discipline.- A strong interest in chirality, molecular ions, ultrafast optics, and scientific instrumentation.- A strong background in atomic, molecular, and optical physics.- Proven experience with experimental laboratory research in one of the following fields: Femtosecond lasers, Ion transfer optics / ion traps, Charged particle detection- Excellent written and spoken English.- Good written and oral communication skills.- An interest in conducting experimental and theoretical research within an interdisciplinary research environment.- Previous experience in chirality, molecular ions, ultrafast optics, or instrumentation will be considered an advantage.- Experience with Python programming is also preferred.MSCA Mobility and Eligibility RequirementsAs the position is funded through the MSCA Doctoral Network, applicants must meet the relevant eligibility requirements.Applicants must satisfy the MSCA mobility rule. In general, candidates must not have resided or carried out their main activity, such as work or studies, in Germany for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately before the recruitment date. Certain exceptions may apply under MSCA rules.Applicants must also be doctoral candidates and must not already hold a doctoral degree at the date of recruitment.Candidates are encouraged to carefully verify their eligibility under the applicable MSCA Doctoral Network conditions before applying.Application DocumentsApplications should include:- Cover letter- Detailed curriculum vitae- Academic transcripts- Copy of the Master's thesis- Scientific publication, if available- Applicants may also optionally include one letter of recommendation.Selection ProcessCandidates will initially be pre-selected based on their qualifications, experience, and suitability for the research project.Shortlisted applicants may then be invited to an online or in-person interview involving representatives from the academic and industrial partners participating in the project.Key InformationPosition: PhD Researcher / Doctoral CandidateNumber of positions: 1Research areas: Physics, Engineering, ChemistryResearcher profile: First Stage Researcher (R1)Contract: Temporary, full-timeWorking hours: 35 hours per weekCountry: GermanyWork locations: Bremen and KasselFunding: Horizon Europe – Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral NetworkProject: TRILOGYMarie Curie Grant Agreement: 101226887If you are interested, please apply online with your CV and Motivation Letter.At Thermo Fisher Scientific, each one of our 100,000 extraordinary minds has a unique story to tell. Join us and contribute to our singular mission—enabling our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer.Thermo Fisher Scientific is an EEO/Affirmative Action Employer and does not discriminate on the basis of  , color, religion, ___ ,   orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or any other legally protected status.Apply today! http://jobs.thermofisher.com (http://jobs.thermofisher.com)

jobs.description: The Max Planck Society is one of the world’s leading research organizations. Its institutes conduct cutting-edge basic research in the natural sciences, life sciences, social sciences and humanities for the benefit of society. Located in Science City Hamburg Bahrenfeld, the Max Planck Institute for the Structure and Dynamics of Matter (MPSD) investigates the properties and dynamics of matter on the elementary timescales of atomic and electronic motion. Its interdisciplinary research combines experimental and theoretical approaches, with a particular focus on ultrafast phenomena, quantum materials and advanced imaging methods. The International Max Planck Research School for Ultrafast Imaging & Structural Dynamics (IMPRS-UFAST) is a joint initiative of the MPSD, Universität Hamburg, Deutsches Elektronen-Synchrotron (DESY) and European XFEL. It provides outstanding doctoral researchers from around the world with a structured and interdisciplinary training environment at the Hamburg-Bahrenfeld research campus.To coordinate and further develop this international doctoral program, the MPSD is seeking a highly motivatedScientific Coordinator (m/f/d) International Max Planck Research School for Ultrafast Imaging & Structural Dynamics (IMPRS-UFAST)The position offers an excellent opportunity to apply academic experience and transferable skills in a new professional context and to develop a career in science management. We are looking for a candidate who understands the opportunities and challenges of doctoral research from personal experience and is motivated to use this knowledge to support and further develop the next generation of international researchers.Your position- Training Programme - Develop and coordinate a semester-based curriculum of scientific courses and transferable-skills training in close collaboration with IMPRS Fellows and Principal Investigators.- Plan and organize workshops, retreats, networking events and career-development activities tailored to the needs of doctoral researchers.- Regularly evaluate and further develop the training program to foster interdisciplinary exchange and professional development.- Annual International Doctoral Recruitment - Coordinate the annual international recruitment and application process, from developing and publishing doctoral projects and launching the call for applications to organizing the selection symposium, conducting interviews and coordinating final admissions.- Doctoral Mentoring and Career Development - Support doctoral researchers throughout their time in the programme, from admission and onboarding through to completion, serving as a trusted contact for programme-related, administrative and career matters.- Develop and coordinate initiatives that help doctoral researchers explore and prepare for career opportunities beyond the PhD.- IMPRS-UFAST Office and Programme Administration - Oversee the day-to-day operations of the IMPRS-UFAST Office and coordinate communication, collaboration and networking among doctoral researchers, academic partners and committees, national and international partner institutions, and the MPSD administration.- Serve as a member of the IMPRS-UFAST Executive Board and contribute to programme governance by preparing and coordinating meetings, implementing decisions, and overseeing reports, evaluations and programme documentation.- Coordinate the programme budget and oversee the website, guidelines, application information, records and communication channels, while contributing to quality assurance, alumni relations, academic networking and the strategic development of IMPRS-UFAST.Your background and skills- A completed doctorate in the natural sciences; postdoctoral experience is an advantage, but not a requirement.- A strong understanding of doctoral research, the challenges and opportunities of an academic career, and the German higher-education and research environment.- A genuine interest in science management and in applying your academic experience and expertise in a broader professional context.- Strong communication, coordination and project-management skills, demonstrated through experience in research, teaching, mentoring, event organisation or collaborative projects.- A proactive, independent and structured approach to work, combined with creativity, initiative and a strong ability to work collaboratively.- Excellent written and spoken English; very good German language skills or a willingness to develop them further are desirable.- Intercultural sensitivity and the ability to communicate and collaborate effectively with doctoral researchers, senior scientists, administrative colleagues and external partners.- Previous experience in science management is an advantage, but not a requirement. We particularly welcome candidates with an academic background who are ready to broaden their professional perspective and bring their scientific expertise, international experience and organisational strengths into a new professional context.Our offer- A varied and rewarding role at the intersection of science, doctoral education, career development and science management, with scope for initiative, professional growth and the opportunity to contribute your own ideas to the further development of IMPRS-UFAST.- An international, interdisciplinary and collegial working environment at the Science City Hamburg Bahrenfeld research campus, with a modern workplace and opportunities for collaboration across institutions.- A wide range of training and professional-development opportunities.- A family-friendly working environment and active support in balancing work, family and personal life.- A subsidy for the Profiticket as a Germany ticket.- Attractive remuneration and social benefits in accordance with the German public pay scale (TVöD Bund), depending on qualifications and professional experience.- Supplementary pension provision through VBL.- An initial contract for two years, with the possibility of permanent employment thereafter.- The Max Planck Society is committed to gender equality, diversity and inclusion. We welcome applications from all backgrounds. The Max Planck Society also aims to increase the number of employees with disabilities and therefore expressly encourages applications from qualified individuals with disabilities.Your applicationPlease submit the following documents through our online application portal by 26 October 2026.- a letter of motivation outlining your interest in science management, doctoral training and the development of IMPRS-UFAST- your curriculum vitae- copies of your relevant university degrees and doctoral certificate- relevant employment certificates or references- a publication list, if applicableFor questions regarding the position, please contact Dr. Neda Lotfiomran (neda.lotfiomran@mpsd.mpg.de (https://mailto:neda.lotfiomran@mpsd.mpg.de) ) .
